human_review: Privacy clocks
The privacy officer decides every breach determination and sends every notice, record copy and review reply; the agents only list the clocks and flag risky words.
Provider pay
The practice administrator checks the RVU file and the comp plan and decides every true-up; the agent does not run payroll.
Compliance pack
The compliance officer confirms every exclusion, licence and health finding against the source and decides what to do; nobody is suspended or terminated by an agent.
Care management
A person checks the time and consent records and decides what to bill; the agents never submit claims or read clinical readings.
Therapy and ABA
The billing lead and the clinicians decide units, modifiers and plan-of-care signatures; the agents never submit claims or read notes.
Hospice and home health
The billing office files every notice and decides on the cap; the agents only list dates and amounts.
Value-based contracts
A person raises roster and payment disputes with the payer after checking the lists; nothing is sent by the agents.
Home care
The agency decides payroll corrections and claim fixes after reading the lists; the agents never submit payroll or claims.
Money recovery
The billing team decides every dispute, appeal, secondary claim, code change and lien reduction; the agents never file, accept or send.
Billing company partner
Each client practice reviews its own lists and settings; every claim, payment, notice and dispute stays with a named person there.
common_problems: Staff, providers or vendors on the OIG exclusion list, and people not screened in the last month.
Licences and BLS cards expired, expiring or never verified, and shifts worked on an expired licence.
Breach notices, HHS reports and state attorney general notices past or close to their deadline.
Patient access requests past 30 days, extensions without a notice, and copy fees above your policy.
Therapy visits past the KX threshold without KX, units over the 8-minute rule, and plans of care unsigned.
Care management and remote monitoring billed with less time or fewer days than the code needs.
EVV visits that do not support the units billed, and caregiver hours paid short.
Surprise-billing negotiation and IDR windows closing or missed, and payments below the QPA.
reaches_the_model: When an AI assistant calls a Fairpractice tool, the agent reads the files on the user's computer and returns a result. Before it leaves the agent, patient, client and member names and numbers, birth dates (cut to the year), phones and e-mails, and the names of providers, therapists, caregivers, employees and reviewers are replaced with stable pseudonyms or placeholders. NPIs, claim and case numbers, codes, dates, amounts and business names such as payers, vendors and law firms are sent as they are; free text such as review texts, reasons and risk plans is sent with known names and phone, e-mail and SSN patterns replaced, and risk owners in the security risk analysis are sent as written. A check of 3,645 masked values in the test files found none in a result. Results go to whatever model the user's assistant uses; for patient data use a model covered by a business associate agreement, or a local model. The reports written on the user's computer keep the real values.
rules_maintained: Every threshold is a named setting in a settings file the customer keeps: 116 settings in 28 agents, 24 of them following a dated rule such as the 60-day HIPAA breach notice, the 30-day right of access, the No Surprises Act 30 and 4 business days, the 5-day hospice and home health notices, the KX threshold and the hospice cap, which CMS sets each year. Each dated default, its source and the date it was checked are listed in docs/settings.md. CPT and CMS time and day rules (care management minutes, remote monitoring days, the 8-minute rule, APCM tiers) are in the agents' code; Mythos Machines changes them, and any default, only in a release with a changelog line, and checking them is part of the support plan.
